name: Natural System of Wrangel Island Reserve
blurb: Polar bear dens, snow geese and a lemming-driven tundra in the high Arctic.

tip.title: Crash the lemmings
tip.text: Set Wrangel Island collared lemming to -100%. Foxes, owls, jaegers and wolverines lose their main prey, and geese nests can become the next target.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Natural System of Wrangel Island Reserve

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Microscopic algae that bloom in the cold, nutrient-rich waters around the island and feed zooplankton and seafloor animals.

nodes.name: Arctic willows
nodes.desc: Dwarf willows such as grayleaf and creeping willow hug the ground. Muskoxen rely on willow most heavily in winter.
Fat-rich zooplankton that graze the phytoplankton bloom and are eaten by Arctic cod and other small sea animals.
The only snow goose population breeding in Asia, nesting in colonies on the island. Nests and goslings are exposed to foxes and jaegers.
Released onto the island in 1975 and now about a thousand strong. Eats grasses and willows; wolves are its main predator elsewhere.

nodes.name: Feral reindeer
nodes.desc: Domestic reindeer brought in during the 1950s now live wild, kept to about 1,000 animals to limit damage to bird nesting grounds.
A small cold-water fish that eats zooplankton and is a main food of ringed seals and many seabirds.
The seal most often taken by polar bears. Its pups wait in snow dens in spring, where Arctic foxes can also reach them.

nodes.name: Pacific walrus
nodes.desc: Wrangel hosts one of the largest walrus gatherings, up to 100,000 on one beach at a time. It dives for clams on the seafloor.
An omnivore for which lemmings are the most common prey. It also takes bird eggs, hunts seal pups and scavenges bear kills.
Breeds in high numbers only when lemmings are plentiful. On Wrangel it can find lemmings tunnelling under the snow by hearing them.
A scavenger and predator that depends heavily on lemmings, and also feeds on carrion and larger animals.
Wrangel has the densest known concentration of polar bear dens. Females den on the island while the bears hunt seals on the sea ice.
The short, bright polar summer powers a brief burst of plant growth on land and plankton blooms at sea.
The surrounding seas are unusually rich in oxygen and nutrients, which supports plankton and the animals above them.
Where algae grow beneath the ice and where polar bears hunt seals. Pack ice also shapes where walruses rest.
